title: Stutters/Frame spikes when using C#
body:
### Tested versions

4.3
4.4.rc2
v4.4.stable.mono

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable.mono - Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) 12 on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (nvidia) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads)

### Issue description

I've posted this as a comment in a separate thread before, but I think this is important enough to lift to it's own thread, as we're getting desperate.

We're currently working on a 3D game and we're doing a lot of physics queries for camera collisions, feelers for adjusting the camera, sight-line checks, IK feet, etc. We realized that we were having a bunch of frame spikes and stutters, and was thinking this was due to the raycasts (maybe 20-30 per frame), which it was to some extent. However we've narrowed down cause for the spikes and all that is required is a single miss in a single script, per frame, for the C# garbage collector to go haywire and cause massive frame time spikes / stuttering.

All it takes is _a single call_ that does a heap allocation per frame. If the game is running enough FPS, this means potentially a couple of hundred times per second which is already reaching the limit of the GC.

This means an innocuous function such as `bool res = Input.IsActionPressed("jump");` might cause stuttering by calling it _once per frame_, since the string is not actually a regular string, but a `StringName` that does heap allocations. Of course, you can cache the StringName, and all is fine and dandy, but this is very easy to miss, and will potentially cause stuttering that is almost impossible to find without proper profiling tools (which are somewhat lacking, both in Godot for C# and for dotnet on Linux in general for example).

This also means that function calls such as `this.GetTree().GetNodesInGroup(groupName);` will also cause frame time spikes and stutters, since this returns a `Godot.Collections.Array` that is likely also HAlloc'd. You can work around this as well by creating your own group system in C#, but at that point we're going out of our way to not use Godot as it's intended to be used.

I understand that maybe calling these functions aren't in you typical "hot-path", but I'm talking about calling them **_once_** per frame. That should be reasonable.

It happens faster if you run uncapped framerate (3000 fps) but it also will likely happen if you run 60 frames per second. For example, try doing 30 raycasts and querying all buttons on 4 gamepads (40 something StringName constructions if they're not cached). That makes for around 4200 potential stutter-inducing calls per second.

I've attached a Minimum reproducing project. It has a single Camera3D that rotates. The script attached to it calls StringName construction and GetNodesInGroup. It causes spikes.
You can change the amount of times the functions are called in the inspector, and also you can enable manual garbage collection in the inspector, which will call `GC.Collect()` once per frame (this halves the framerate, but removes the spikes).
I've tested it on Windows 11, and Debian 12, both with the same result. I've also tested both 4.3 and with 4.4 rc2.

I'm hoping this is just us having missed a performance checkbox and there's a quick fix, but I'm really worried that this is something that won't be possible to improve before our release (about a year away maybe?).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fbcfc43-baf9-4780-9bd6-f13240a4a049)

### Steps to reproduce

Call `bool res = Input.IsActionPressed("jump");` or `this.GetTree().GetNodesInGroup(groupName);` or any other function that returns a Godot.Collection type, once per frame.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

MRP: [TestGC.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19015834/TestGC.zip)

(MRP is made in 4.4.rc2.mono)
